note: San Onofre State Beach's inland campground, in a chaparral canyon beside the dry San Mateo Creek wash about a mile east of I-5. A 1.5-mile nature trail runs down the creek to the Trestles surf break. Paved back-in sites; showers take tokens. The gate is open 6 am to 10 pm. --Claude
summary: parks.ca.gov page and restrictions, ReserveCalifornia facilities and unit details, imagery read. Open, year-round. 60 water/electric (30 A) sites at $70 and 30 standard sites at $45, same rate year-round; 101-157 are tent sites. RC caps every unit at 25 ft (page text says 36 ft). Not waterfront confirmed (dry wash, ocean ~2 km). Pin fine. Website line 2 to drop.
flags: RIG LENGTH CONFLICT: ReserveCalifornia caps every San Mateo unit at VehicleLength 25 ('Site Length 25'; E/W pads 32 ft, standard pads 24 ft), and the parks.ca.gov summary box says 'Max trailer: 25 feet' / 'Max camper/motorhome: 25 feet', but the page's camping text says 'Bluffs and San Mateo Campgrounds : 36 Feet'. Written 25 (the booking limit). A 23-ft rig fits either way.

SITE COUNT: 157 -> 90. RC types 101-157 as 'Tent Primitive Campsite' and 68-100 as standard sites with 'Standard: Tent' but VehicleLength 25 and paved back-in drives; counted 60 + 30. If the reviewer reads 68-100 as tent-only, the count is 60.
WEBSITE: line 1 https://www.parks.ca.gov/sanonofre works (-> ?page_id=647), keep it; line 2 https://www.reservecalifornia.com is the generic home, so drop it.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront agrees. San Mateo Creek is a dry sandy wash on imagery, and the ocean is ~2 km away by a 1.5-mile trail under I-5, so not coastal walk.

CROSS-ENTRY: the San Onofre Bluffs campground is already entry 11706 (RC facilities 674-682, primitive sites at 25 ft, no hookups). Parts of the Bluffs south of the Trail 1 lot are closed after the Scales Fire (parks.ca.gov post 144), worth checking when 11706 comes up.
